sonata-form.short: Sonata form presents themes in different keys, develops them, then brings them back around the home key.

exposition.short: An exposition introduces the main themes of a sonata-form movement or the first round of subject entries in a fugue.

development.short: The development is the middle section of a sonata-form movement, where earlier themes are altered and taken through other keys.

recapitulation.short: The recapitulation brings back a sonata-form movement’s opening themes, usually with the later themes now in the home key.

coda.short: A coda is a closing passage added after a piece’s main sections, ranging from a few chords to a substantial final section.

rondo.short: A rondo brings its main tune back between contrasting episodes, often in the pattern A–B–A–C–A.

ternary-form.short: Ternary form has an opening section, a contrasting middle and a return of the opening, often with changes.

binary-form.short: Binary form divides a piece into two main sections, usually repeated, with the second bringing the music home.

theme-and-variations.short: Theme and variations presents a tune followed by altered versions that retain something of its melody, bass or chords.

fugue.short: A fugue builds a piece from a theme that enters in successive voices and returns throughout the music.

subject.short: A fugue subject is the main melody that the different voices introduce and repeatedly take up.

answer.short: A fugal answer repeats the subject in another voice, usually a fifth higher or a fourth lower.

countersubject.short: A countersubject is a recurring melody designed to accompany a fugue’s subject or answer.

episode.short: An episode is a passage between statements of a fugue subject or returns of a refrain.

stretto.short: Stretto overlaps entries of a fugue subject, with the next voice starting before the previous statement has finished.

ritornello.short: A ritornello is a returning instrumental passage, often the orchestral refrain between solo episodes in a Baroque concerto.

passacaglia.short: A passacaglia builds continuous variations over a recurring bass line or sequence of chords.

chaconne.short: A chaconne is a set of variations built on a recurring bass or chord pattern, usually in triple time.

scherzo.short: A scherzo is a lively piece or movement, often in triple time with a contrasting middle section called a trio.

minuet-and-trio.short: A minuet and trio pairs two contrasting dances in triple time, then repeats the minuet.

toccata.short: A toccata is an instrumental showpiece, usually for keyboard, built around the player’s touch and dexterity.

fantasia.short: A fantasia is a freely shaped piece that often sounds improvised, with sudden changes of pace and direction.

prelude.short: A prelude is an introductory piece, or a self-contained piece that keeps the freedom of an introduction.

nocturne.short: A nocturne is a night piece, most often a lyrical piano work with a singing melody over flowing chords.

lied.short: A Lied is a German-language song, especially an art song for solo voice with piano or orchestra.

aria.short: An aria is a substantial solo song in an opera, oratorio or cantata.

recitative.short: Recitative is singing shaped by the rhythm of speech, often used for dialogue or narrative.

symphonic-poem.short: A symphonic poem is a usually single-movement orchestral work inspired by a story, poem, picture or idea.

programme-music.short: Programme music is instrumental music linked to a story, scene or other subject beyond the music itself.

concerto.short: A concerto brings one or more soloists into musical partnership and competition with an orchestra.

tonic.short: The tonic is a key’s home note, and the tonic chord is the chord built on that note.

dominant.short: The dominant is the fifth note of a key, or the chord built on it, which commonly leads back to the tonic.

modulation.short: Modulation is a change from one established key to another within a piece.

cadence.short: A cadence is a melodic and harmonic arrival that marks the end of a phrase or section.

pedal-point.short: A pedal point is a note held or repeated while the chords around it change.

neapolitan-sixth.short: A Neapolitan sixth is a major chord on the flattened second note of a key, with its third in the bass.

augmented-sixth.short: An augmented sixth chord contains two notes that usually move outwards by a semitone to an octave on the dominant.

diminished-seventh.short: A diminished seventh chord consists of four notes a minor third apart, making a tense chord with several possible resolutions.

tristan-chord.short: The Tristan chord is the unsettled F–B–D♯–G♯ chord heard near the opening of Wagner’s Tristan und Isolde.

chromaticism.short: Chromaticism uses notes outside the prevailing scale, often bringing semitone movement into melodies and chords.

atonality.short: Atonality is music without an established home key or the usual pull of dominant chords towards a tonic.

twelve-note-row.short: A twelve-note row places the twelve notes of the chromatic scale in an order that supplies a piece’s melodies and chords.

modes.short: Modes are ways of arranging a scale around a home note, each with its own pattern of tones and semitones.

whole-tone-scale.short: A whole-tone scale has six notes, with a whole tone between every neighbouring pair.

octatonic-scale.short: An octatonic scale has eight notes, with tones and semitones alternating.

bitonality.short: Bitonality places two keys side by side in the same passage.

suspension.short: A suspension holds a note from one chord into the next, where it clashes before resolving down by step.

appoggiatura.short: An appoggiatura is a leaning note that delays a chord note, usually on a strong beat, then resolves by step.

modal-mixture.short: Modal mixture borrows notes or chords from the major or minor scale that shares a piece’s tonic.

lament-bass.short: A lament bass descends from the tonic to the dominant, often repeating beneath a song of grief.

counterpoint.short: Counterpoint combines melodic lines that keep their own shape and rhythm while sounding together.

imitation.short: Imitation occurs when one voice repeats a melody or fragment just heard in another voice.

canon.short: A canon is a melody followed by another voice that keeps imitating it at a fixed distance in time.

homophony.short: Homophony gives one melody the lead while the other parts supply its harmony.

ostinato.short: An ostinato is a short musical pattern repeated persistently while the music around it changes.

motif.short: A motif is a short, recognisable musical idea that can be repeated, altered and combined with other ideas.

leitmotif.short: A leitmotif is a recurring musical idea associated with a character, object or thought in a drama.

cyclic-form.short: Cyclic form links the movements of a work by bringing back themes heard in earlier movements.

orchestration.short: Orchestration assigns music to instruments and combines their sounds.

divisi.short: Divisi tells the players in an instrumental section to divide between separate parts.

pizzicato.short: Pizzicato means plucking the strings of a bowed instrument with a finger.

tremolo.short: Tremolo is the rapid repetition of a note or rapid alternation between notes.

col-legno.short: Col legno tells string players to use the wooden stick of the bow against the strings.

ornament.short: An ornament is a note or group of notes that decorates and shapes a melody.

rubato.short: Rubato is expressive flexibility of timing, with some notes lingering and others moving ahead.

metre.short: Metre groups musical beats into recurring patterns, such as the three beats in a waltz.

polyrhythm.short: Polyrhythm combines different divisions of the same span of time, such as two even notes against three.

bar.short: A bar is a span of music between bar lines, normally containing the number of beats shown by the time signature.

catalogue-number.short: A catalogue number identifies a particular work within a composer’s output.

equal-temperament.short: Twelve-note equal temperament divides the octave into twelve equal semitones, giving every key the same pattern of intervals.

well-temperament.short: Well temperament is a family of unequal keyboard tunings that makes every key usable while giving different keys different interval sizes.

concert-pitch.short: Concert pitch is the agreed reference pitch to which musicians tune their instruments.

clavichord.short: A clavichord is a quiet, touch-sensitive keyboard instrument whose metal tangents strike the strings and remain against them.

basset-clarinet.short: A basset clarinet extends the clarinet’s range downwards to written low C.

basso-continuo.short: Basso continuo is a bass line with chords supplied by a keyboard or plucked-string player, often joined by a bass instrument.

period-instruments.short: Period instruments are instruments of a historical period, or copies built to its designs.

acoustic-recording.short: Acoustic recording uses a horn and diaphragm to move a cutting stylus directly, without microphones.

78-rpm.short: A 78 rpm record is a disc designed to turn at roughly seventy-eight revolutions per minute.

matrix-number.short: A matrix number identifies a recording master, while an accompanying take number distinguishes separate attempts.

transfer.short: A transfer copies sound from one medium to another, such as an old disc into a digital file.

public-domain-audio.short: A work in the public domain is free of copyright protection in the country concerned.

level-trace.short: A level trace is a graph showing the changing strength of the sound captured in a recording.

score-alignment.short: Score alignment matches places in a written score to the moments when they are played in a recording.

quotation.short: A musical quotation brings a recognisable passage from an existing tune or work into another piece.

parody.short: Musical parody can mean reworking an existing composition or imitating music for comic effect.

modelling.short: Modelling uses another work’s musical plan or pattern as a starting point for a new composition.

homage.short: An homage is a piece written in honour of someone, sometimes borrowing their style or favourite forms.

transcription.short: A transcription adapts a piece for different instruments or voices.

evidence-status.short: Evidence status tells the reader whether a claim is documented, inferred or disputed.

perfect-cadence.short: A perfect cadence closes a phrase by moving from the dominant chord to the tonic.

half-cadence.short: A half cadence ends a phrase on the dominant chord, leaving the music poised to continue.

deceptive-cadence.short: A deceptive cadence sends the dominant to an unexpected chord, usually the chord on the sixth degree, delaying the close.

plagal-cadence.short: A plagal cadence moves from the subdominant chord to the tonic, as in many settings of ‘Amen’.

elision.short: Elision overlaps the end of one musical phrase or section with the beginning of the next.

pivot-chord.short: A pivot chord belongs to both the old key and the new one, helping the music pass between them.

common-tone-modulation.short: Common-tone modulation connects keys through a note that belongs to both the departing and arriving harmonies.

direct-modulation.short: Direct modulation moves into a new key without a connecting passage or pivot chord.

enharmonic-reinterpretation.short: Enharmonic reinterpretation gives a note or chord a new spelling and harmonic role while keeping its sounding pitch.

chromatic-slide.short: A chromatic slide shifts a note or chord by a semitone into a new harmonic setting.

sequence.short: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at successively higher or lower pitches.

dominant-pedal.short: A dominant pedal holds or repeats the fifth note of the key while the music above it changes.

tonic-pedal.short: A tonic pedal holds or repeats the home note while the chords and melodies around it move.

retransition.short: A retransition leads back from a contrasting passage to the return of familiar opening music.

standing-on-the-dominant.short: Standing on the dominant prolongs dominant harmony while the melody and rhythm continue to move.

liquidation.short: Liquidation gradually removes a motif’s distinctive features until only a simple figure or chord remains.

motivic-link.short: A motivic link carries a recognisable musical fragment from one phrase or section into the next.

fermata.short: A fermata is a sign that extends a note, chord or rest beyond its written duration.

general-pause.short: A general pause is a rest for the whole ensemble at once.

medial-caesura.short: A medial caesura is the break between the transition and the second theme in a sonata exposition.

crescendo-build.short: A crescendo build is a passage that grows gradually louder towards a climax.

decrescendo.short: A decrescendo gradually makes the music quieter.

texture-change.short: A texture change alters the number of musical lines or the way they fit together.

orchestration-change.short: An orchestration change gives the music to different instruments or alters their combination.

register-change.short: A register change moves the music into a higher or lower pitch range.

tempo-change.short: A tempo change alters the speed of the musical beat.

metre-change.short: A metre change alters the grouping or division of the beat, usually shown by a new time signature.

link-passage.short: A link passage connects two musical phrases or sections.

cadenza.short: A cadenza is a solo display, usually unaccompanied, within a concerto, aria or other work.

attacca.short: Attacca tells performers to continue straight into the next movement or section without a break.

fade.short: A fade-out ends a passage by making its sound gradually disappear.
